problems.title: Initial-condition replay and stored-action replay are different actor updates
problems.source_location: Sections 2.4 and 3.3, PDF pp. 4–5; Appendix C, Algorithm 2, PDF p. 19.
claim: The body says current-policy rollouts restart from sampled contexts; Algorithm 2 instead loads a saved trajectory and updates its stored actions without behavior correction.
analysis: In a one-step bandit, let rewards be \(1,0\), current good-action probability \(0.2\), replay good-action probability \(0.9\), and action-independent critic baseline \(2\). The true current-policy logit gradient is \(0.2(0.8)=0.16\). Reusing stored actions instead gives \(0.9(0.8)(-1)+0.1(-0.2)(-2)=-0.68\). An action-independent baseline cancels under on-policy sampling; it need not cancel under the replay law. Terminal masking permits this one-step case within a longer maximum imagination horizon.
result: The two written algorithms are not generally equivalent. The witness does not show that the actual experiments used old actions or encountered this state; original implementation/logs are needed for that determination.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Make the pseudocode match initial-context replay with fresh current-policy actions, or specify and justify the off-policy alternative. No performance-preserving drop-in repair is established.

problems.title: Accumulated positive TD residuals and their mean reverse rankings
problems.source_location: Eq. (7), PDF p. 5; Appendix C, Algorithm 2, PDF p. 19; horizon interpretation, PDF pp. 8 and 20.
claim: Eq.(7) sums future discounted positive TD residuals for every starting position; Algorithm 2 takes their plain mean.
analysis: For horizon \(H=5\), \(q=0.985\cdot0.95=0.93575\), and positive TD residual vectors \(A=(0.9,0,0,0,0)\), \(B=(0,0,0.75,0,0)\), plain means are \(0.18,0.15\). The accumulated future-residual score instead gives \(0.18\) and \(0.15(1+q+q^2)=0.421706709375\), reversing their ranking. Binary terminal rewards and value estimates in \([0,1]\) can realize these vectors; the witness does not require illegal reward timing.
result: The priorities are different functions, even at equal horizon; endpoint indexing cannot resolve the reversed ordering. A horizon trend under the accumulated form can partly reflect its position weights, rather than independently demonstrating difficulty.
assumptions: The finding concerns the stated source version and mathematical or released-code scope.
repair: Specify which of the two priority functions is intended. Changing horizon normalization also changes the curriculum; no benchmark-equivalent substitution is asserted.
